payout_quote: How much do e-jurors get paid? For each verdict rendered, eJurors are paid $5 - $10 depending on the length of the case. The amount to be paid will be shown at the top of each case. (eJury's published FAQ, as mirrored; eJury's own juror page confirms the case mechanics: attorney posts facts and jury questions, eJurors review and click Submit Verdict, minimum ~50 verdicts per case)
timing: Payment via PayPal after the case concludes (once the minimum ~50 verdicts are in)
eligibility: 18+, US citizen, able to read and write English, sound mind and good moral character, no felony convictions, not under indictment, not a practicing paralegal/legal assistant/insurance adjuster and not working with an attorney or law firm
steps: Register as an eJuror on eJury with your county and demographics
Wait for an email notification when a case posts in your county
Log in, read the case facts and answer the jury questions plus personal questions
Receive $5-$10 via PayPal once the case concludes
catches: Cases are NOT steady work - frequency depends entirely on how many attorneys in your county use eJury; outside Dallas/Tarrant County, Texas it can be months between cases
Cases are first-come, first-served: once 50 verdicts are in, the case closes and late jurors earn nothing
US citizens only; legal professionals and anyone with a felony are excluded
You are an independent contractor - no taxes withheld, report the income
Payment only arrives after the case concludes, not the moment you submit
